title: Gödel Incompleteness via Turing Undecidability
description: A fully constructive, 0-axiom formalization of the Turing route to Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem: undecidability of a diagonal (halting-style) predicate forces incompleteness of any sound, effectively axiomatized theory that represents it. The independent sentence is produced explicitly by diagonalizing against the theory's own provability decider — the recursion-theoretic Gödel sentence 'the prover rejects its own code'. 7 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Kurt Gödel (1931), Alan Turing (1936); recursion-theoretic synthesis formalized in Lean 4

mathlibDependencies.description: General tactic library (simp, cases, omega) and core Bool/logic lemmas

originalContributions: D_undecidable: the Turing/Cantor diagonal in its purest form — no code in the family ℕ → ℕ → Bool decides the self-rejection predicate D n := (run n n = false), uniform over every choice of run
SoundEffectiveTheory: an abstract structure capturing a sound, effectively axiomatized theory of the diagonal sentences (soundness on both sides + provability decided by a code)

godel_via_turing: the headline — every such theory has an EXPLICIT independent sentence, with the witness being the code of the theory's own provability decider (the recursion-theoretic Gödel sentence)
godel_sentence_independent: isolates D e (e = code of the provability decider) as the concrete Gödel sentence delivered by the Turing route
incompleteness: the same fact restated as ¬ Complete, paralleling the parent's first_incompleteness but as a theorem about ALL sound effective theories rather than one fixed encoding
sound_imp_consistent: soundness alone already yields consistency (no sentence both provable and refutable)
no_decider_for_const_true: a concrete instance showing the obstruction is structural, not about the predicate being 'hard'

overview.historicalContext: In 1931 Gödel proved that any consistent, effectively axiomatized theory strong enough for arithmetic is incomplete, building a self-referential sentence by hand via the diagonal lemma. In 1936 Turing proved the halting problem undecidable. The two results are the same diagonal argument viewed from two angles: Turing's undecidability immediately yields incompleteness, because a complete sound theory whose theorems are recursively enumerable would decide the undecidable. Kleene's recursion-theoretic proofs of incompleteness (1936–1943) made this bridge canonical, and it is the form in which the theorem is usually taught in computability courses today. This file formalizes that bridge directly and constructively.
overview.problemStatement: Show that undecidability of a diagonal predicate forces incompleteness: for any sound, effectively axiomatized theory T of the self-rejection sentences D n := (run n n = false), exhibit an explicit sentence neither provable nor refutable in T, and conclude ¬ Complete T for every such T.
overview.proofStrategy: Two parts. Part I proves the abstract diagonal D is undecidable: if some code e were its characteristic function, evaluating at the diagonal n = e yields run e e = true ↔ run e e = false, a Boolean with no fixed point. Part II packages a theory as a SoundEffectiveTheory structure (provability, refutability, two soundness fields, and an effectiveness field giving a decider code for provability) and diagonalizes against that decider: the sentence D e (e = the provability decider's own code) cannot be provable (soundness would make run e e = false while the decider says true) and cannot be refutable (soundness would make D e true again), so it is independent — hence the theory is not complete. Part III instantiates the diagonal at the constant-true family to show the obstruction is structural, not about D being 'hard'.
overview.keyInsight: One never needs to construct a Gödel sentence by hand. Diagonalizing against the provability predicate ITSELF produces an explicit independent sentence, and the witness is simply the code e of the theory's own provability decider: the sentence D e says 'the prover rejects its own code', which is true precisely when it is unprovable.
keyInsights: **Incompleteness is a corollary of undecidability, not a separate construction.** A complete, sound, effectively axiomatized theory would let you decide the undecidable diagonal predicate D, so no such theory can be complete — the entire syntactic fixed-point apparatus is bypassed.

**The Gödel sentence is handed to you for free.** The witness is the code e of the theory's own provability decider; the sentence D e ('the prover rejects its own code') is true exactly when unprovable, mirroring the classical fixed point G ↔ ¬Prov(⌜G⌝) without any diagonal lemma.

**Soundness alone already gives consistency.** sound_imp_consistent needs neither effectiveness nor the diagonal: if a sentence were both provable and refutable, the two soundness fields would make D n simultaneously true and false. Only incompleteness requires the diagonal.

**The result is universally quantified over theories.** Where the parent proves incompleteness for one fixed encoding with a placeholder provability predicate, godel_via_turing and incompleteness hold for ALL sound, effectively axiomatized theories of the D-sentences — assumptions live in the SoundEffectiveTheory hypothesis, not as global axioms.

**The obstruction is structural.** no_decider_for_const_true shows even the empty predicate is undecidable inside a family closed under self-application: undecidability comes from the diagonal closure of run, not from the predicate being computationally hard.
overview.significance: Connects the parent gallery proof's syntactic incompleteness (a fixed encoding with placeholder provability) to the recursion-theoretic viewpoint, proving incompleteness as a theorem quantified over ALL sound, effectively axiomatized theories of the diagonal sentences.

mainTheorems.name: GodelTuring.D_undecidable
mainTheorems.description: No code decides the diagonal (halting-style) predicate D n := (run n n = false). This is the Turing/Cantor diagonal, uniform over every run.
mainTheorems.leanStatement: theorem D_undecidable : ¬ ∃ e, DecidedBy run (D run) e

mainTheorems.name: GodelTuring.godel_via_turing
mainTheorems.description: Every sound, effectively axiomatized theory of the D-sentences has an explicit independent sentence; the witness is the code e of the theory's own provability decider.
mainTheorems.leanStatement: theorem godel_via_turing (T : SoundEffectiveTheory run) : ∃ n, ¬ T.Provable n ∧ ¬ T.Refutable n

mainTheorems.name: GodelTuring.incompleteness
mainTheorems.description: A sound, effectively axiomatized theory of the D-sentences is never complete.
mainTheorems.leanStatement: theorem incompleteness (T : SoundEffectiveTheory run) : ¬ Complete T

mainTheorems.name: GodelTuring.godel_sentence_independent
mainTheorems.description: The independent sentence is D e with e the code of the provability decider — the explicit recursion-theoretic Gödel sentence.
mainTheorems.leanStatement: theorem godel_sentence_independent (T : SoundEffectiveTheory run) (e : ℕ) (he : DecidedBy run T.Provable e) : ¬ T.Provable e ∧ ¬ T.Refutable e

mainTheorems.name: GodelTuring.sound_imp_consistent
mainTheorems.description: Soundness alone yields consistency: no sentence is both provable and refutable.
mainTheorems.leanStatement: theorem sound_imp_consistent (T : SoundEffectiveTheory run) (n : ℕ) : ¬ (T.Provable n ∧ T.Refutable n)

crossReferences.description: The parent builds incompleteness syntactically via the diagonal lemma with a placeholder provability predicate; this file derives incompleteness from Turing-style undecidability for all sound effective theories.
Both exhibit an explicit undecidable sentence; here it is the diagonalization of the provability decider rather than a fixed Gödel code.

conclusion.summary: Incompleteness need not be built by hand: it is a corollary of Turing's diagonal. Any sound, effectively axiomatized theory that represents the self-rejection predicate D fails to decide the sentence D e, where e is the code of its own provability decider. The whole development is constructive and 0-axiom (the only foundational dependency is propext, in D_undecidable, which does not count as an assumption under the axiom-integrity policy).
conclusion.implications:
**1. Unifies two pillars of logic.** Gödel's incompleteness and Turing's undecidability are exhibited as one diagonal argument, with the Gödel sentence reduced to a special case of the halting diagonal.

**2. Explicit, not merely existential.** The independent sentence is named (D e, e = the provability decider's code), so the theorem delivers a concrete witness rather than an abstract existence claim.

**3. Honest scope.** run is modelled as a total Bool-valued family, which suffices for the diagonal but is not the genuine partial-recursive halting problem; the SoundEffectiveTheory hypothesis abstracts arithmetization rather than performing it, so this complements — not replaces — the parent's syntactic construction.
conclusion.futureDirections: Replace the total-Bool family run by Mathlib's partial-recursive functions (Nat.Partrec) to recover the genuine halting problem, and connect SoundEffectiveTheory to a concrete arithmetised provability predicate to close the loop with the parent's syntactic Gödel sentence.
openQuestions: Can SoundEffectiveTheory be instantiated by a concrete arithmetised theory (e.g. Robinson Q or PA over Mathlib's first-order logic) so that godel_via_turing yields the standard Gödel sentence rather than an abstract D e?

Does replacing the total run : ℕ → ℕ → Bool by Nat.Partrec partial functions recover Turing's halting problem verbatim, and what is the minimal soundness hypothesis under which the bridge still holds?
Can the same diagonal framework be pushed to Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem — formalizing that a sound effective theory cannot prove its own consistency statement?
